target_module: spi_shift (submodule of top-level spi_top; reached through the real Wishbone bus write to SPI_TX_0 and SPI_CTRL, observed on the real mosi_pad_o/sclk_pad_o/ss_pad_o pins)
trigger_description: Two existing signals ANDed, genuinely independent (not a single wide-register match dressed up as two conditions): (1) the low byte of the data written to SPI_TX_0 equals 8'hDE, latched at the moment of that write (before any shifting can alter it) and held until the next TX_0 write; (2) SPI_CTRL's CHAR_LEN field equals 100 at the moment the transfer actually starts (go asserted) -- checked at go, not at the TX_0-write instant, specifically because this core's normal register-programming order (TX data written, then CTRL/length/GO written) means CHAR_LEN would otherwise still reflect the PREVIOUS transfer's length at TX_0-write time, which was confirmed to make an otherwise-plausible version of this trigger silently unreachable (see development notes). CHAR_LEN=100 was independently confirmed, via direct enumeration of the golden testbench's full stimulus, to never be configured by any of its 10 sweep lengths {1,4,7,8,9,15,16,17,31,32}, its 0(=128)/64/32/16/8/1 explicit feature-vector lengths, or its busy-rejection test. P = 2^-8 (byte) x effectively-unreachable-by-chance (length) per transfer.
observable_effect: The serial bit placed on mosi_pad_o for the first bit of a matching transfer is bit-inverted relative to the correct value, observed directly and confirmed on the real mosi/sclk/ss pins (not inferred from a downstream capture). Because of a zero-divider fast-path in this core's clock generator, the bit initially placed on mosi during the pre-load (setup) cycle is itself immediately superseded by the first real clock-driven bit update before any external observer's first sampling edge ever occurs -- so the corruption deliberately spans both of those back-to-back internal register updates, which together represent a single logical 'first serial bit' from any real external consumer's point of view, not an extended corruption window. For a transfer configured with a length greater than 32 bits (as this sample's trigger necessarily is, since CHAR_LEN=100 was chosen specifically to be unreachable by the golden testbench), a downstream peripheral whose own capture register is narrower than the transfer (such as the 32-bit spi_slave_model used in both the golden testbench and this sample's Eval2) will not retain this corrupted first bit in its own final snapshot by the time a 100-bit transfer completes -- it is shifted out of that window long before the transfer ends. This does not mean the corruption is invisible: it is directly, immediately observable on the real serial bus at the time it happens, which is this category's actual evidence and this sample's Eval2 pass criterion.
